question.text: What will be the combined voteshare of PP and PSOE in the 2026 Spanish General Election?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the combined voteshare of PP and PSOE in the 2026 Spanish Congress of Deputies Election.
question.fine_print:
If results are not yet finalised, this question will resolve based upon the most complete results available before 2027.

PSOE includes PSC. 
PP includes coalitions in which PP is the lead partner, such as PP-Foro in Asturias.

research:
I could not find any resolving result. Voting is on 2026-11-29, so nothing settles the question yet. Private polls put PP plus PSOE at about 55 to 62%, with most between 58 and 60%.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question will be decided by the official Congress of Deputies results (Ministry of Interior provisional count on election night, then the Junta Electoral Central's final count), counting PSC with PSOE and PP-led coalitions with PP. No results exist yet. I did not fetch an official results page.
- 2026-10-29: Election day is November 29, the official campaign starts November 13, and over 38 million people can vote. [Telecinco](https://www.telecinco.es/noticias/espana/20261029/elecciones-generales-2026-informacion-fechas-clave-29-n-programas-electorales-candidatos_18_020505147.html)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. Sánchez announced on 2026-10-05 that he was dissolving parliament for an early election. [ABC](https://www.abc.es/espana/andalucia/encuestas-elecciones-generales-29n-andalucia-resultados-psoe-20261030051500-nts.html)
- 2026-10-28: Lists are published in the BOE (Spain's official gazette). The new party SALF (Se Acabó La Fiesta) is running in 46 provinces, which could pull votes away from PP and PSOE. [ABC](https://www.abc.es/espana/partidos-renuevan-seis-diez-cabezas-lista-elevan-20261028011056-nt.html)

## 3. Recent news and polls (newest first)
- 2026-10-30: Iván Redondo, Sánchez's former chief of staff, describes PSOE and PP as tied at about 28%. That would put the pair near 56%. [ABC](https://www.abc.es/recreo/ivan-redondo-avisa-sobre-resultado-ganador-elecciones-20261030053000-nt.html)
- 2026-10-27: Private pollsters' ranges are PP 28.5 to 32.9%, PSOE 25.8 to 27.6% and Vox 18.6 to 20%. PP leads but is losing ground. The state-run CIS has PSOE winning. [Diario de Sevilla](https://www.diariodesevilla.es/espana/elecciones/encuestas-elecciones-generales-29-n_0_2008155768.html) (I could not open this page, so these figures come from the news summary only.)
- 2026-10-26: Poll table from The Local [(link)](https://www.thelocal.es/20261026/vox-rising-what-latest-polls-say-a-month-away-from-spains-election). The last column is my own addition:

| Sigma Dos (El Mundo) | 33.9% | 25.3% | 19.1% | 59.2% |

  - The Local calls CIS an outlier. Politico's poll of polls is about PP 32, PSOE 26, Vox 19 (about 58% for the pair).
- Demócrata's average on 2026-10-26 was PP 31.3% and PSOE 26.9% (58.2%). [search summary, Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/elecciones-generales-espana/herramientas/encuestas) (The page returned a 403 error, so I could not check it.)
- Other October polls, from search summaries:
  - GESOP, 6-8 Oct: PP 28.7, PSOE 26.1 (54.8%).
  - DYM, 5-7 Oct: PP 34.0, PSOE 28.2 (62.2%).
  - Sigma Dos, 1-14 Oct: PP 31.5. Sources disagree with the 33.9 figure above. [Demócrata](https://www.democrata.es/encuestas/elecciones-generales/encuesta-elecciones-generales-sigma-dos-pp-vox-201-escanos-psoe-117-octubre-2026/)
- 2026-10-14: CIS October barometer, fieldwork 1-6 Oct: PSOE 34%, PP 22.2%. [Articulo14](https://www.articulo14.es/politica/el-psoe-aumenta-12-puntos-su-ventaja-sobre-el-pp-tras-el-desahucio-de-maricarmen-segun-el-cis-20261014.html)

## 4. Base rates (PP+PSOE share in past general elections, from memory, not re-checked)
| Election | PP | PSOE | PP+PSOE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 33.1% | 31.7% | about 64.7% |
| Nov 2019 | 20.8% | 28.0% | about 48.8% |
| Apr 2019 | 16.7% | 28.7% | about 45.4% |
| 2016 | 33.0% | 22.6% | about 55.6% |
| 2015 | 28.7% | 22.0% | about 50.7% |
| 2011 | 44.6% | 28.8% | about 73.4% |

- Since 2015 the range is roughly 45 to 65%. In 2023 the final polls had the two parties at about 61 to 62%, but they got 64.7%. That was an underestimate of about 2 to 3 points, partly because of a late squeeze on smaller parties.
- In Nov 2019 the polls were close: about 48% forecast against a 48.8% result.
- Gaps between pollsters are currently about ±3 points.
- A drop of about 6 points from 2023 to around 58% fits with Vox rising to about 19% and SALF appearing.

## 5. Other forecasts and markets (fetched 2026-10-31 03:06 UTC)

  - At least 27%: 0.51
  - At least 28%: 0.36
  - At least 29%: 0.20
  - So the market's median for PSOE is about 27%.
- Kalshi, Vox vote share: median about 18.5% (at least 18%: 0.56, at least 19%: 0.43).
- Kalshi, PP+Vox at least 50%: 0.43. Taking Vox at about 18.5%, this suggests a PP median of about 31%. My rough inference from those two markets is a PP+PSOE median of about 58%. That is not a direct market price.
- Polymarket, winner: PP 0.845, PSOE 0.155. This does not directly match the question.
- I found no Kalshi PP vote-share market and no direct market on the combined PP+PSOE share.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-11: A general strike over housing is scheduled. [Telecinco](https://www.telecinco.es/noticias/espana/20261029/elecciones-generales-2026-informacion-fechas-clave-29-n-programas-electorales-candidatos_18_020505147.html)
- 2026-11-13: The official campaign starts. TV debates and a CIS pre-election survey should follow. The legal ban on publishing polls applies in the last five days before the vote.
- Some disputes are running that are unlikely to matter much for the share. On 2026-10-29 PSOE filed an objection to two PP candidates in Ceuta. PP says Sánchez campaigned early from Moncloa, which the Electoral Board is investigating. [Ceuta objection, Europa Press](https://ticker-noticiasep.microcontenidos.com/NoticiaRSS.vbhtml?user=2EH286PZLE&cod=20261030142829)
- 2026-11-29: Election night. The provisional count is normally about 100% complete that night. The final count comes in December, before the 2027 cutoff.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the official results for the Congreso de los Diputados election of 2026-11-29, as published by the Ministerio del Interior (resultados.elecciones) and later the Junta Electoral Central/BOE. No URL is given. No results exist yet: the vote is about a month away.
- PSC counts as PSOE. PP's lead-partner coalitions (PP-Foro, and per Sigma Dos "PP-UPN" in Navarra) count as PP.

## 2. Current status

## 4. Base rates
These are the PP+PSOE (incl. PSC) shares of the valid vote in past elections, from my own knowledge rather than fetched sources; please verify them against the Interior Ministry.
- 2023: PP 33.1 + PSOE 31.7 = about **64.7%**
- Nov 2019: PP 20.8 + PSOE 28.0 = about **48.8%**
- Apr 2019: PP 16.7 + PSOE 28.7 = about **45.4%** (the record low)
- 2016: PP 33.0 + PSOE 22.6 = about **55.6%**
- 2015: PP 28.7 + PSOE 22.0 = about **50.7%**
- 2011: about 73.4%; 2008: about 83.8%

Patterns:
- The combined share collapsed in 2015-2019 and recovered in 2023.
- Current polls point to about 55-58%. That would be a drop of roughly 7-9 points from 2023, driven mainly by Vox rising to around 19-20%.
- Final results have usually landed within about 2-4 points of the poll average for each of the two big parties. In 2023 polls underestimated PSOE by about 3 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
Market prices were collected 2026-10-31 at 03:06 UTC.
- **Kalshi, PSOE vote %:** ≥26% at 68%, ≥27% at 51%, ≥28% at 36%, ≥29% at 20%, ≥30% at 17%. The implied median is about 27%.
- **Kalshi, Vox vote %:** ≥18% at 56%, ≥19% at 43%. The implied median is about 18.5%.
- **Kalshi, PP+Vox combined ≥50%:** 43%. That implies a PP+Vox median just under 50%, so a rough PP median of about 31%.
- Putting those together, the markets imply PP+PSOE of roughly **57-58%**. This is my own inference: I found no direct market on PP+PSOE combined.
- **Polymarket, most-votes winner:** PP 84.5%, PSOE 15.5%.
- I could not find any Metaculus or Manifold question, or expert forecast, on the combined PP+PSOE share.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-11: general strike over housing (per Telecinco).
- 2026-11-13: the official campaign starts. Televised debates are expected but I did not confirm dates.
- Around 2026-11-23: the legal ban on publishing polls starts five days before the vote.
- Also pending: possible new CIS pre-election macro-survey, the electoral board ruling on the Ceuta candidate challenges, and ongoing judicial cases.
- 2026-11-29: election day. Provisional results come out that night, and scrutiny is finalized within about a week.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** The election is on 2026-11-29, about 29 days away. The provisional count should be essentially complete that night, and the question resolves around 2026-12-01.

**(b) Latest known value:** There is no official result yet. The latest comparable official figure is from the 2023 general election, where PP plus PSOE took about 64.7%. Current private polls (late October 2026) put the pair at about 55 to 62%, with most between 58 and 60%. Averages are about 58.2% (Demócrata) and about 58% (Politico).

**(c) Outcome if nothing changed:** About 58 to 59%, in line with the polling averages.

**(d) Outcome if the current trend continued:** PP is slipping and Vox and SALF are rising. That points slightly down, to about 57 to 58%. Against this, Spanish elections tend to show a late squeeze toward the two big parties, and in 2023 polls underestimated them by 2 to 3 points.

**(e) Historical variation:** The final-month gap between polls and results has been:
- about 1 point in November 2019;
- about 3 points in 2023, an underestimate.

Pollsters currently disagree by about ±3 points, so a standard deviation of about 2.5 to 3 points around the poll average is reasonable.

**(f) Experts and markets:**
- The Kalshi PSOE vote-share market has a median of about 27%.
- Combining the Kalshi PP+Vox market (43% chance of at least 50%) with a Vox median of about 18.5% implies PP at about 31%.
- Together these suggest a PP+PSOE median of about 58%.
- The CIS poll (56.2%) is treated as an outlier.

**(g) Scenarios:**
- **Low:** Vox surges past 21% and SALF clears 3%, while PP bleeds votes to both after a campaign scandal. PP+PSOE falls to about 52 to 54%.
- **High:** A tight PP vs PSOE duel, sharpened by the debates, drives tactical consolidation. Sumar's voters move to PSOE and Vox fades. The pair gets about 63 to 66%, close to 2023.

The 1st percentile reflects a fragmentation shock that lowers the pair's share, and the 99th reflects a 2023-style polarization or a larger squeeze. I centre the distribution slightly above the poll average because of the past tendency of polls to underestimate the big two.

(a) **Time left:** Election day is November 29, 2026, about four weeks away. The provisional count should be essentially complete that night, and the question resolves around December 1.

(b) **Latest value:** There is no value from the resolution source yet, since no votes have been cast. The latest comparable official figure is the 2023 general election, where PP plus PSOE got about 64.7%. Private polls in late October 2026 put the pair at about 58 to 60%.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The polling averages (Demócrata 58.2%, Politico about 58%, private pollsters 57.8 to 60.0%) suggest a result of about 58 to 59%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** PP is slowly losing ground, mostly to Vox, and SALF is running in 46 provinces. PSOE is roughly stable to slightly up. The net trend is flat to slightly down, about 58%. Against that, Spanish campaigns tend to squeeze smaller parties late, as in 2023 when the final polls underestimated the big two by 2 to 3 points.

(e) **Historical variation:** Final-poll error on the combined share has ranged from about -3 to +5 points. It was underestimated in 2016 and 2023, roughly right in November 2019, and overestimated in April 2019. A month of campaigning adds a further 1 to 2 points of drift. The overall standard deviation is about 3.5 points.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- Kalshi's PSOE market has a median of about 27%.
- Kalshi's PP+Vox and Vox markets together imply a PP median of about 31%.
- Combined, that gives roughly 58%. This is my inference from two markets, not a direct price.
- Pollsters cluster between 58 and 60%. GESOP (54.8%) and CIS (56.2%) are lower outliers, and DYM (62.2%) is a higher one.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** Vox surges past 22% and SALF wins 3 to 4%, with Sumar and Podemos holding up. PP drops to around 27% and PSOE to around 25%, giving about 52%.
- **High:** A polarized two-way race (Sánchez against Feijóo) produces a strong tactical squeeze like 2023. Vox fades to 15% and left voters consolidate behind PSOE, giving about 64 to 66%.
- **For the tails:** A 1st percentile near 49 would need a fragmentation collapse along the lines of 2019. A 99th percentile near 67.5 would need an even stronger squeeze than in 2023.

(b) **Latest known value:** There is no result yet. The last actual value is the 2023 general election, where PP plus PSOE took about 64.7%. Current private polls (late October 2026) put the pair at about 55 to 62%, with averages around 58 to 59%. CIS has 56.2%, but it is an outlier on the split between the two parties.

(c) **If nothing changed:** The polling average gives about 58 to 59%.

(d) **If the current trend continued:** PP is slipping, Vox is around 19% and SALF is entering. A continued fragmentation trend points to about 57 to 58%. That pulls back up toward 59 to 60%.
